- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later — suggest adjusting for a downward bias in the middle-to-late period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 90+), model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect, leading to prolonged overestimation — apply a dampening factor or lagged smoothing after spikes.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model fails to recognize that prices often revert to prior 10–15 day averages after volatility — incorporate moving average or volatility-adjusted mean reversion in calibration.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent underestimation of true values — especially in the last 10 days — suggest adding a “tail correction” or “late-period bias” adjustment.
- Model exhibits strong lagged behavior — forecasts often lag true values by 2–5 days — consider incorporating a 1–3 day lagged true value as a smoothing or calibration anchor.
